 Sharad Kapoor's health struggles prompt AICWA to write to PM Narendra Modi, seeks pension scheme for film workers
 SECTIONS Sharad Kapoor's health struggles prompt AICWA to write to PM Narendra Modi, seeks pension scheme for film workers By ET Entertainment Desk , Last Updated: Nov 18, 2026, 02:39:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Actor Sharad Kapoor's health struggles and appeal for work have prompted AICWA to write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking a national welfare fund and pension scheme for film workers. AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta proposed 'Cine Aashray Kosh', highlighting the lack of job security, pensions and medical support for thousands of cinema workers.
 AICWA approaches PM Narendra Modi after Sharad Kapoor's health struggles, seeking financial security and pensions for film industry workers. 
 Sharad Kapoor’s recent viral video drew attention to his physical ailments as the actor appealed to the industry to give him work. The actor, who has worked with superstars like Shah Rukh Khan in Josh, Salman Khan in Jai Ho, and Hrithik Roshan in Lakshya, recently opened up about injuring his foot while playing football in Barcelona. His health has suffered, forcing him to give up his four pet dogs to a care center. Now, the All Idian Cine Workers Associated (AICWA) shared a letter addressed to PM Narendra Modi, urging the government to create a national welfare fund and pension scheme for cinema workers.
 The association says Sharad's situation highlights a much bigger problem affecting thousands of industry professionals.
 AICWA writes to PM Narendra Modi, seeks pension scheme for artists
"No artist should be left alone in their worst hour," the association wrote on Instagram, as they shared the photos of the letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Highlighting the difficulties faced by workers behind the scenes, AICWA said, "Behind the screen, thousands of artists and workers of Indian cinema have no pension, no job security and no safety net when work, health or age turns against them." The association added, "We must make sure there is no other Sharad Kapoor tomorrow." 
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by All Indian Cine Workers Association (@aicwaofficial) 
 AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has requested the Prime Minister to establish the 'Cine Aashray Kosh', a national welfare fund for artists and workers in Indian cinema, along with a pension scheme. The association also appealed to the film industry to support its members, stating, " Cine Aashray Kosh is the need of the hour. The Government must act at the earliest." It further asked, "If we do not stand by our own, who will?"
 Sonu Sood and Salman Khan offer aid
As per reports by ABP Live, Salman Khan had reached out to his Jai Ho co-star Sharad Kapoor to check on his well-being and even assured him financial support. Meanwhile, Sonu Sood too has reportedly extended medical aid for Sharad Kapoor by sending out a team of doctors to look after Kapoor's leg injury. The medical team would arrange the necessarily treatment for the Josh actor.
